Exploring a one-person company model supported by a Cardano stake pool and sharing practical experience.
Through our work, we hope to make Cardano new infrastructure for one-person companies.

c1.title: AI lowers the operating threshold
c1.body:
Product development, content, and daily operations have traditionally required several people. AI tools reduce some of that time and labor, allowing one person to handle more of the work.
They do not replace every role, but they expand what an individual can reasonably operate.

c2.title: A company needs recurring revenue
c2.body:
Nodes, servers, and AI services create fixed expenses. Relying only on one-off projects makes long-term product maintenance difficult.
Revenue from the pool, products, consulting, and investments helps cover the company’s operating costs.

c3.title: Cardano staking creates a clear relationship
c3.body:
Delegators do not transfer custody of their assets or purchase a separate subscription. Their ADA remains in their own wallet and continues to earn protocol staking rewards.
Pao Pool earns pool revenue and provides delegators with corresponding member content and product benefits.

model.title: Revenue Mix
model.summary: For a one-person company, survival comes first. Pao Studio aims to use pool operating revenue as its main source for covering basic expenses, while continuing to explore income from trading, value-added product services, consulting, and project development.

perks.title: Stake to subscribe
perks.sub:
Traditional subscriptions require users to pay recurring fees. Pao Studio is testing a new subscription model based on Cardano native staking.
For most ADA holders, participating in staking means delegating to a stake pool. Users delegate ADA to Pao Pool with no additional payment, lock-up, or custody, while continuing to receive staking rewards as usual. Pool operating revenue keeps Pao Pool running and supports the content and product services provided by Pao Studio.

i1.title: No separate subscription fee
i1.body: ADA is not transferred to Pao Studio or Pao Pool and is not locked during delegation.

i2.title: Delegation represents membership
i2.body: On-chain delegation status can identify members and provide access to relevant content, product features, early releases, and member events.

i3.title: Pool revenue supports operations
i3.body: Pao Pool operating revenue pays for nodes, servers, AI services, and product development, providing one source of income for the one-person company.

i4.title: Delegators take part in product iteration
i4.body: Delegators can test early products and submit actual requirements. That feedback informs product adjustments.

tier.body: No separate subscription fee is required. Delegating ADA to Pao Pool provides access to the content and product services we offer.

step4.title: Confirm Transaction
step4.description: Enter the amount you want to stake and the reward receiving address, click "Delegate" and confirm the transaction to start earning rewards.

immutableSpec.description: Keeps people and AI working from the same spec and linked documents, with every plan, decision, outcome, and piece of validation evidence recorded as the project evolves.

challenge.description: Before implementation starts, check whether the problem is real, the solution is unnecessarily complex, and its key assumptions actually hold.

codebaseDesign.description: Define module responsibilities and interactions before writing code, so complexity stays in the right place and the system remains easier to change and test.

tdd.description: Work one behavior at a time: write a failing test first, then add only enough code to make it pass.

codeReview.description: Have three isolated reviewers inspect the same changes independently, then verify and merge their findings for a human to decide what to address.

codebaseMap.description: Maintain a concise map of important directories, module responsibilities, and entry points so people and agents can find their way through the codebase quickly.
